inputs.sbc_source: 10-K equivalent (FY2026 Annual Report note 'Share-based payments expense' $104m, cash-flow add-back note 'Share-based payment transactions'); no equity-award withholding tax line disclosed separately (EquityAwardTaxes KPI is 0 every year) so cash-flow add-back is the combined figure
inputs.share_count_basis: 1,135,283 thousand ordinary shares on issue at FY2026 year-end (30 June 2026), FY2026 Annual Report note 'Shares on issue'; held FLAT because SBC (immaterial at 0.22% of revenue) is fully expensed in the flows and there is no material non-SBC dilution (no buybacks, no equity raises)
inputs.wacc_rationale: AUD flows discounted at an AUD-built WACC. 8.0% reflects Wesfarmers' investment-grade credit profile (Moody's A3 stable / S&P A- stable, S&P debt/EBITDA downside threshold relaxed to 3.0x in Jul-2026), diversified low-cyclicality retail core (Bunnings/Kmart ~68% of revenue) against an AU risk-free rate ~4.3% and an AU equity risk premium ~5-6%; set below the folder's single-commodity AU cyclicals (BAP.AX, BSL.AX use higher WACC/mid-cycle treatments) because WES's conglomerate structure diversifies segment-level cyclicality (retail resilience offsetting WesCEF commodity/lithium volatility) and its 42-year capital-allocation record reduces execution risk relative to a single-business industrial.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B) — leases as operating cost. FY2026 cash-flow statement shows lease INTEREST ($309m) already inside operating activities (deducted reaching OCF of $4,272m) but lease PRINCIPAL ($1,098m) sits in financing activities, NOT deducted from OCF -- so reported FCF is flattered by the undeducted principal, exactly the AASB16 trap the method flags. Modelled the full lease payment (principal+interest, ~3.0% of revenue, stable FY2024-26 at 2.98-3.20%) as an explicit lease_cost_pct_path deducted from EBITDA-equivalent, used D&A EX-ROU ($717m FY2026 = $574m PP&E + $143m intangibles, excluding $1,127m ROU depreciation) for the EBIT/cash-tax calc, and EXCLUDED lease liabilities ($7,070m FY2026) from net_debt (net_debt uses interest-bearing loans and borrowings only, $5,646m, matching the CSV's TotalDebt which the parser already keeps ex-lease).
inputs.nci_treatment: No material NCI disclosed at group level; consolidated NetIncome is fully attributable to Wesfarmers shareholders (no NCI deduction line in the income statement). Equity-accounted associates and JVs (BWP Group 23.44% stake, Covalent Lithium 50% JV with SQM, Flybuys 50%, Wespine 50%, book value $1,058m at FY2026) are carried at equity method with 'Share of net profits of associates and joint ventures' ($126m FY2026) already consolidated INSIDE reported EBITDA/NI -- this income was NOT stripped from the flows, so per the matching-asset rule its book value was correspondingly NOT added to the equity bridge (adding it would double-count an income stream still inside the projected flows).
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF DCF, component-built margins, 10-year horizon (owner-FCF margin still normalizing off a FY2027 capex step-up, so a 5yr Gordon capitalization would freeze an immature margin). Diversified ASX conglomerate (Bunnings 43%, Kmart Group 25%, Wesfarmers Health 14%, WesCEF incl. lithium 7%, Officeworks 8%, Industrial & Safety 4% of FY2026 revenue) -- routed via SKILL.md to owner-FCF DCF + non-US/cyclical adaptations (references/owner-fcf-adaptations.md) for the lease treatment and WACC-currency items; not a REIT/bank/LIC despite the conglomerate structure because the group consolidates operating retail/industrial P&Ls, not a portfolio of fair-valued assets or deposits. Coles demerger (Nov-2018) breaks continuity before FY2019: FY2016-2018 include Coles and are EXCLUDED from historical growth calculations; FY2019 headline NetIncome ($5,510m) is inflated by the discontinued-ops gain on demerger, so NetIncomeContinuing ($1,940m FY2019) is the clean base for the post-demerger series (FY2019-FY2026, 7 years). AASB16 lease accounting starts FY2020, handled via the lease_cost_pct_path/net-debt treatment above rather than excluded from history, since the FY2020-26 window is internally consistent. FY2022 ($2,267m) and FY2026 ($1,249m distribution, described in the FY2026 results commentary as a combined ~$1.7bn capital return + special dividend across the H1/H2 payment) capital returns are financing distributions to shareholders, NOT ordinary dividends and NOT deducted from owner FCF -- they affect share count/equity only via the (unmodelled, since share count is held flat and no buyback occurred) capital structure, not the operating flow build. FY2023 revenue step-up ($36,838m -> $43,550m) is the API/Priceline (Wesfarmers Health) acquisition -- consolidated into the FY2023+ revenue base used for growth, not adjusted out, since it is now a permanent segment. Equity/book-value CAGR is NEGATIVE (-3.9% 5yr) purely because of the FY2022 and FY2026 capital returns (~$3.5bn total distributed back to shareholders on top of ordinary dividends) -- this is a capital-allocation choice, not business shrinkage, so growth is anchored on revenue-continuing (+6.9% 5yr) and NetIncomeContinuing (+3.8% 5yr) CAGRs instead; see historical_growth.notes.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: blend of revenue_5yr_cagr (6.85%, inflated by the FY2023 API/Priceline acquisition step-up) and NetIncomeContinuing 5yr CAGR (3.84%); selected 4.0% year-1 base growth as the organic-plus-bolt-on run rate, decelerating to 2.5% terminal
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity/book-value CAGR (-3.9% 5yr) diverges sharply (>30%) from revenue (+6.9% 5yr) and NI-continuing (+3.8% 5yr) CAGRs -- driven entirely by ~$3.5bn of capital returns (FY2022 $2,267m, FY2026 $1,249m) distributed on top of ordinary dividends, not by earnings deterioration. Equity CAGR is therefore NOT used as the growth anchor; owner-FCF CAGR is also negative (-8 to -10%) purely because AASB16 lease principal (excluded from pre-2020 reported FCF, included in the post-2020 comparison basis via this build's lease treatment) and the FY2027 capex step-up depress the recent owner-FCF base -- also not used as the growth anchor, only as the margin-build starting point.

base.narrative: Base case: Bunnings and Kmart Group keep taking share on everyday-low-price positioning and digital/marketplace expansion at mid-single-digit growth; WesCEF/Covalent Lithium ramps through FY2027 odour-mitigation and becomes a modest steady contributor at nameplate-adjacent output; Officeworks/Industrial-and-Safety transformation stabilises rather than re-accelerates; FY2027's guided capex step-up ($1.3-1.5bn net) normalises back toward the historical ~2.6% of revenue by year 5 as Mt Holland expansion and Built Living JV initial build-out complete; margins hold flat-to-slightly-improving as OneDigital/retail-media monetisation offsets cost-of-doing-business inflation; balance sheet stays within the relaxed 3.0x debt/EBITDA covenant headroom.

bull.narrative: Bull case: Covalent Lithium refinery ramp-up clears the odour-mitigation issues faster than guided, offtake qualification completes on schedule, and lithium prices recover, turning WesCEF/lithium into a genuine second growth engine; OneDigital's retail media network and agentic-commerce (Buddy/Joy/Ollie) initiatives scale into a high-margin monetisation layer faster than expected; Bunnings' commercial/trade segment gets a tailwind from an earlier-than-guided residential construction recovery; Blackwoods/Workwear integration into Bunnings from FY2027 delivers cost synergies ahead of plan; Wesfarmers Health's Priceline-led consumer transformation accelerates margin expansion; ACCC Bunnings-Uber Eats scrutiny resolves without material constraint.

bear.narrative: Bear case: Australian consumer/cost-of-living pressure and subdued residential construction persist multiple years, dragging Bunnings commercial and Kmart/Target discretionary sales growth to near-flat; Covalent Lithium's odour-mitigation and recovery-rate problems extend well past FY2027 with a soft lithium price cycle, keeping the segment a earnings drag rather than a contributor and forcing further capex without a return; ACCC finds against the Bunnings-Uber Eats arrangement, constraining commercial practices and inviting broader market-power scrutiny that pressures Bunnings' margins; Officeworks and Target underperformance persists, absorbing ongoing transformation spend without earnings recovery; elevated net debt/equity (66.1% post FY2026 capital return) and higher finance costs compound margin pressure; cost-of-doing-business inflation (labour, energy) outpaces productivity offsets.

scenario_narratives.base: Diversified conglomerate compounds at a mid-single-digit blended rate as mature retail (Bunnings/Kmart, ~68% of revenue) grinds out share gains while WesCEF/lithium normalises into a modest contributor after the FY2027 capex step-up; margins hold broadly flat to slightly improving on digital/retail-media monetisation.
scenario_narratives.bull: Lithium ramp-up and OneDigital monetisation both inflect faster than guided, turning two emerging platforms into real growth engines alongside continued Bunnings/Kmart share gains and an earlier residential-construction recovery.
scenario_narratives.bear: Soft Australian consumer spending, a stalled lithium ramp, and adverse ACCC findings on Bunnings' market power compound with elevated post-capital-return leverage and rising finance costs to compress margins for several years running.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: House default 15/50/35 adjusted: bear weight raised to 20% (from 15%) given genuine near-term execution risk stacking up together -- lithium refinery commissioning delays already realised (odour issues pushing ramp-up to H2 FY2027), elevated leverage post the FY2026 $1.7bn capital return (net debt/equity 66.1%, debt/EBITDA 1.9x) just as FY2027 finance costs and capex both guided higher, plus live ACCC antitrust scrutiny of Bunnings; bull weight trimmed to 30% (from 35%) because the bull case needs multiple independent things to go right simultaneously (lithium AND OneDigital AND construction recovery) rather than one clear catalyst.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Wesfarmers is valued as a single consolidated owner-FCF DCF, not sum-of-parts, because its divisions report into one consolidated P&L and cash flow statement and the group's stated identity IS the capital-allocation function connecting them (42-year track record of rotating out of declining businesses and into new ones) -- unlike a REIT/funds-manager stapled structure or a holdco with separately-listed pieces, there is no natural place to split the valuation. The single largest historical discontinuity is the November 2018 Coles demerger: FY2016-2018 (Coles included) are excluded entirely from growth/margin history, and FY2019's headline net income is a one-off demerger-gain artefact, so the clean historical base for this build is the post-demerger NetIncomeContinuing/revenue-continuing series, FY2019-FY2026. The other structural adjustment is AASB16 leases (from FY2020): the cash-flow statement shows lease interest already inside operating cash flow but lease principal sitting in financing and NOT deducted, which flatters reported FCF by ~$1.0-1.2bn/year; this build corrects for that with an explicit lease-cost-as-%-of-revenue deduction (treatment B) and D&A ex-right-of-use for the tax calculation, while keeping lease liabilities out of net debt to avoid double-counting. A 10-year horizon is used because the FY2027 guided capex step-up ($1.3-1.5bn net vs $779m FY2026, driven by Mt Holland lithium expansion and the new Built Living JV) means the owner-FCF margin has not yet reached a mature run-rate at year 5; the capex_pct path tapers back toward the historical ~2.6% of revenue by around year 5-6. Growth is anchored on revenue-continuing and NetIncomeContinuing CAGRs (6.9% and 3.8% over 5 years) rather than equity/book-value CAGR, which is negative (-3.9%) purely as an artefact of the FY2022 and FY2026 capital returns (~$3.5bn combined distributed back to shareholders on top of ordinary dividends) -- a capital-allocation choice, not business contraction.
key_risks_to_valuation: Covalent Lithium refinery ramp-up execution risk (odour mitigation, recovery rates below design through FY2027, offtake qualification pending) could keep WesCEF/lithium a capital-intensive drag well past this model's assumed normalisation

ACCC antitrust scrutiny of the Bunnings-Uber Eats exclusive delivery arrangement could constrain Bunnings' commercial practices or invite broader market-power findings that compress the group's largest and most profitable segment's margins

Elevated post-capital-return leverage (net debt/equity 66.1%, debt/EBITDA 1.9x) combined with guided-higher FY2027 finance costs reduces balance sheet flexibility just as capex is stepping up, raising the cost of any further downside surprise
Officeworks and Target (within Kmart Group) remain structurally weaker performers requiring ongoing transformation spend without a clear inflection point in this build's base case

The lease treatment (B) and the Coles-demerger historical exclusion are both judgment calls with real magnitude -- a reader who prefers treatment (A) or wants FY2016-18 included would get a materially different owner-FCF base
